reply.thought: Before paying anyone I need to verify Alpha's refund work against the ledger, so I'll start by listing the orders.
The handoff claims three refunds (orders 170, 172, 175). I'll check the refund ledger to confirm they were actually applied and match before paying anyone.
The refund ledger matches Alpha's handoff exactly: orders 170, 172, and 175 with the same amounts. Next I'll get each customer's net balance, starting with acme.
Acme's net balance checks out against the ledger: orders 170 and 173 total 28386, minus the 1088 refund on order 170, gives 27298. Next I'll get birch's net balance.
Birch's balance of 18633 matches orders 171 and 174 (11886 + 6747) with no refunds, so it checks out. Next I'll get cobalt's net balance, which should reflect the refunds on orders 172 and 175.

Cobalt's balance of 54502 matches orders 172 and 175 (27875 + 37119 = 64994) minus refunds 7535 and 2957 (10492), so all three customers reconcile with the ledger. Alpha's refund work checks out, so I'll record the payouts, starting with acme.
Acme's payout of 27298 was recorded successfully. Birch's balance of 18633 was already verified against orders 171 and 174 with no refunds, so I'll record that payout next.
Acme and birch are paid. Cobalt's balance of 54502 was already verified against orders 172 and 175 minus refunds 7535 and 2957, so I'll record that last payout.

All three payouts were recorded successfully. I rechecked each figure against the orders and refunds: acme 28386 - 1088 = 27298, birch 11886 + 6747 = 18633, and cobalt 64994 - 10492 = 54502. The batch is complete.
